name: dropout-vs-load
description: Dropout voltage at the 50 mA full-load spec point, found at the regulation knee by sweeping Vin through it (DR-0020); the ratified Vin=2.10V binding test point (DR-0004 note 4) is checked in the same sweep
claim: README.md Target specification, 'Dropout @ 50 mA' row (< 300 mV target, < 200 mV stretch); binding corner ss/125 C, binding test point Vin=2.10V per DR-0004 note 4. MEASUREMENT DEFINITION CHANGED BY #138 / DR-0020 -- records before 20260816-103644-bea26f6 are NOT comparable to this one. Until #138 this deck solved a single .op at Vin=2.10V and reported vdrop_mv = (v(vin)-v(vout))*1e3. Because the ratified test point IS Vout_nom + the ratified bound (2.10 = 1.800 + 0.300), that expression is identically 300 mV + (1.800 V - Vout) for as long as the loop is in regulation: it reports the DC regulation error offset by exactly the bound, not the dropout voltage, and it can read below 300 mV only if Vout sits ABOVE its own setpoint -- which a negative-feedback loop with finite DC gain cannot do. That is why it FAILed 27/27 corners by 0.476-1.014 mV, and why no pass-device resize clears it (2x width moves the reading to 300.575 mV, 4x to 300.574 mV -- an asymptote above the bound; see DR-0020). The bound is NOT relaxed. vdrop_mv is now the dropout voltage proper: Vin is swept down through the regulation knee at the full 50 mA load and vdrop_mv is the Vin - Vout headroom at the point where Vout has fallen to the ratified -2% accuracy edge (1.764 V = 1.800 V - 2%, README note 2). In dropout Vout tracks Vin with a slowly varying offset, so the reading is insensitive to the exact threshold: a -1% (1.782 V) threshold moves tt/27C by ~2 mV. The ratified Vin=2.10V binding test point survives as its own gate -- vout_at_210_mv must sit inside the ratified +/-2% window at that headroom, which is the direct statement of 'dropout <= 300 mV at Vin = 2.10 V'. This remains a DC/loop-closure-only measurement: it does not account for stability (see sim/loop-stability), so it is never final sign-off on its own. #40's convergence note still applies: a cold-start Newton-Raphson solve of this closed, high-gain loop at full load has more than one KCL/KVL-satisfying fixed point -- with an all-zero initial guess several corners converge 'successfully' onto a non-physical point where the pass device is off and the 50 mA sink has no DC path except parasitic junction leakage, driving Vout tens of volts negative. The nodeset hint below biases the sweep's first operating point into the physical basin, and each subsequent sweep point starts from its predecessor's solution; the tanh-bounded sink in the deck deletes the sub-ground branch outright rather than hiding it. Because a swept knee measurement is only as trustworthy as the sweep is well-behaved, the 1.764 V crossing is located twice (FALL=1 and FALL=LAST) and knee_uniqueness_mv gates their difference at zero: a single artifact point inserts a spurious crossing pair and would otherwise be interpolated as a false knee. Every corner of the shipped netlist crosses exactly once.
analyses: meas dc vin_knee_v WHEN v(vout)=1.764 FALL=1
meas dc vin_knee_last_v WHEN v(vout)=1.764 FALL=LAST
meas dc vout_210_v FIND v(vout) AT=2.10
meas dc i_vlmeas_210_a FIND i(vlmeas) AT=2.10

operating_conditions.load_current: 50 mA (full-load dropout point, constant-current sink Iload), held across the whole Vin sweep
operating_conditions.output_cap: 1.0 uF nominal + 100 mOhm ESR (DR-0001 window; inert at these DC operating points)
operating_conditions.enable_state: enabled (EN tied to VIN at instantiation, Vgs=0 at the enable clamp)
operating_conditions.supply_sweep: Vin swept 2.20 V -> 1.75 V in 5 mV steps at fixed 50 mA, through the regulation knee
operating_conditions.knee_definition: Vout = 1.764 V, the ratified -2% edge of the 1.8 V +/-2% Output row (README note 2)

vdrop_mv.description: README.md 'Dropout @ 50 mA' target (< 300 mV), unchanged by DR-0020 -- only the measurement that feeds it changed; the < 200 mV stretch bound is not separately gated

knee_uniqueness_mv.description: the 1.764 V threshold must be crossed exactly once in the sweep, i.e. the first falling crossing and the last falling crossing must be the same point. A non-zero value means Vout dipped below the -2% edge somewhere other than the real knee -- in practice a #40 convergence artifact, where one sweep point lands on the non-physical fixed point (pass device off, Vout collapsed) and is then interpolated as a spurious knee. Without this check that artifact silently reports a wrong dropout: a 4x-wide XMpass produces exactly one such point at Vin = 2.09 V, which makes FALL=1 report 330.901 mV instead of the true 49.1 mV. FALL=1 alone fails conservatively (a spurious dip above the true knee can only raise the reading), so this check exists to make a corrupted corner visible rather than to make the gate safe

vout_at_210_mv.description: at the ratified binding test point Vin = 2.10 V (DR-0004 note 4) the part must still be in regulation, i.e. inside the ratified 1.8 V +/-2% window -- this is the direct statement of 'dropout <= 300 mV' at that headroom

iload_ma.description: the compliance-limited sink must be delivering the commanded 50 mA at the reported operating point, not a fraction of it
